doc.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998

title: Building Bob Wilber's career
summary: She took on promoting Bob's career, writing NEA grants, driven by tenacity and her northern English upbringing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Right. You seem to make a good pair. And I know over the twenty years you’ve had quite a significant hand in Bob’s career. Did you, when you first got into trying to further his career, was it a steep learning process for you, of how to negotiate contracts and how to open avenues? How to get him in other parts of the world that he hadn’t been in before?

No. Because tenacity is my middle name. And I felt when I got to know Bob better, that he was far more — he was deserving of far more than he’d actually achieved. When he was young he had a lot of acclaim with The Wildcats and with the bands that he had, and I think he went into a sort of period of what I thought was something semi-obscurity, which I thought was unfair, and I thought that we had to dig really fast in order to make up for lost time. And at that point I took on a lot of chores that I didn’t expect to take on, but because I felt that he was worth it, and I felt that the world should know how worth it he was. That’s my role in life I think. I mean I can sing, I can get up and sing, Bob always laughs, he says she doesn’t need to rehearse you know. I mean I’ll tackle “Lush Life” or anything you want me to sing, but I’m much more interested in being a husband builder. And my husband I think is really worth it. And so I found that everything came

to me. I wrote four grants for him to the NEA and got them for him, because I felt that he certainly is passing on a legacy, just as one was passed on to him. I think that Hamilton in bestowing this honorary doctorate on him have done a very wise thing. I know they’ll never regret it. And so for me, life has always been hurdles. I love them. I think that it’s just something to do. I mean you don’t just look at it and say well what should we do, you get on with it. And I think that’s part of my north country upbringing. I think Marian McPartland, I mean I know you endowed her with an honorary doctorate, Marian is from the same kind of stock you know. You don’t just stand there. I mean we English have had to stand up to a lot. And so Bob was a challenge and Bob’s career was challenge to me. I didn’t know how to deal with all these things, but you learn. We all had the tools.
